chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Musa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He disliked that the game be shot while it is leading (or grazing) in the Sanctuary (Haram).

key_terms.الْحَرَمَ: the Sanctuary (specifically the Haram of Mecca)
key_terms.يَؤُمُّ: leading or grazing (in the context of animals in a sacred area)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hunting game within the sacred precincts of Mecca according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expresses dislike (*karah*) for hunting game while it is in the state of *imam* (likely referring to *muhrim* or being in the sacred precincts) within the Haram, highlighting the sanctity of the area. This ruling underscores the specific prohibitions and conditions applied to hunting within the boundaries of Mecca, distinguishing it from general hunting laws. The scholarly context emphasizes the reverence for the Haram as a zone where normal activities are restricted to preserve its spiritual purity.
